title: Plant Disease, HLVd & Biosecurity
level: Plant Health, IPM & Biosecurity Specialist / advanced specialization development
intendedAudience: Learners progressing through the Plant Health, IPM & Biosecurity Specialist pathway
Cultivation personnel responsible for disease scouting, clean-stock verification, containment, testing escalation and biosecurity records
prerequisites: Scouting Systems & Diagnostic Reasoning or equivalent advanced diagnostic foundation
evidencePolicy: Plant-disease and HLVd claims are grounded in cannabis-specific peer-reviewed literature and controlled greenhouse disease-management sources. Visual symptoms alone are not treated as proof of pathogen identity or pathogen-free status, and laboratory methods, sanitizers, quarantine criteria and release rules remain controlled by validated facility procedures.
assessmentPolicy: The dedicated specialist assessment is development-only until exact-version technical/assessment review, accessibility review and pilot evidence are complete. Course completion does not authorize pesticide selection/application, laboratory diagnosis, quarantine release or destruction decisions.
description: Develops specialist disease and biosecurity reasoning for cannabis, including biotic-versus-abiotic differentials, root/crown disease, powdery mildew and Botrytis risk, HLVd transmission/testing concepts, clean-stock controls, containment and reconstructable biosecurity records.
learningOutcomes: Differentiate disease signs, symptoms and abiotic look-alikes using distribution, plant part, environmental/root-zone context and confirmatory evidence before assigning cause.
Analyze major cannabis root/crown, foliar and flower disease risks using pathogen, host, environment and process evidence while preserving diagnostic uncertainty.
Explain HLVd biology, asymptomatic infection, transmission pathways, testing limits and clean-stock implications without treating visual inspection as a reliable exclusion test.
Design a layered biosecurity response for suspect plant material using movement control, separation, sanitation, sampling/testing escalation, traceability and controlled release authority.
Produce a reconstructable disease/biosecurity investigation record that distinguishes observation, hypothesis, test result, containment action, disposition authority and unresolved follow-up.
